newsitem.title: New Zealand: Feltex returning to NZ ownership - NZPA.
newsitem.headline: Feltex returning to NZ ownership - NZPA.

text.p: Feltex Carpets is believed to be about to return to New Zealand ownership after seven years in overseas ownership, the New Zealand Press Association reported on Tuesday.

BTR Nylex, which bought Feltex Carpets as part of Feltrax International from Equiticorp in 1989, is close to selling it to a new company called Feltex Carpets Holdings, which comprises senior management and investment bank CS First Boston, the New Zealand Herald reports.
It is understood that Chris Davis, present general manager of Feltex Carpets, will head the new company.
The sale, rumoured since September, follows the recent sale of Feltex Industrial Textiles to Donaghys for an undisclosed price.
Feltex Carpets comprises wool scouring, yarn spinning, rubber underlay and carpet making and distribution businesses.
Likely buyers for the carpet company included Cavalier Corporation, and Australian company Godfrey Hirst, but a management buyout was always the most likely outcome, industry sources said.
Feltex Carpets is believed to hold about 30 percent of the New Zealand carpet market.

BTR is selling Feltex as part of its divestment of non-core businesses. The British company is retaining businesses in which it says that it can be a world player,'' including packaging and engineered automotive and aerospace products.
